ON THE 12th OF NOVEMBER, 2024
MISC .
CRIMINAL CASE No. 28235 of 2024
MILAN GIRI  Versus
THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH

Appearance:
 Shri Vasant Roland Daniel, Sr. Advocate with Shri Aad  Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Hemant Sharma, Government Advocate with Shri Vir  Panel Lawyer for the non-applicant/State.
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C./482 of BNSS seeking anticipatory bail by the applicant/accused, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR/Crime No.17/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Crime Branch, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable u/S 409 and 420/34 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station - Crime Branch, District Indore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Prosecution story, in brief is that Kalptaru Grih Nirman Sarkari Sanstha Maryadit (hereinafter referred to as the "Society") is a registered Housing Development Cooperation.

entities.text: Kalptaru Grih Nirman Sarkari Sanstha Maryadit
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Last election of the Board of Directors was conducted on 16.08.2017.
Sub-Auditor Suresh Bhandari NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:32166 2 MCRC-28235-2024 was appointed as the Administrator of the society.
Thereafter, when Suresh Bhandari checked the accounts of the Society, he found major financial irregularities and embezzlement of huge amount.

It was also found that a sum of Rs.4,89,27,472/- was embezzled in favour of Board of Directors, co-accused Dilip Sisodia, who was Ex-President and present applicant, who was also a Director of the Society.

On the basis of written complaint filed by Suresh Bhandari, on 03.04.2023, an FIR was lodged against present applicant and co-accused person and members of the Board of Directors i.e., Chairman Kamlesh Jain, Deputy Milan Giri vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117670516/

sentences.text: Chairman Sunny Jaiswal, Jeetendra Narayan Patel, Subhash Kanhaiyalal Patidar, Darshan Pratap Singh Mehta, Shri Chanda, Jeetendra Patil, Smt. Madhukanta and Dilip Sisodia.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is further submitted that present applicant was Director of the Society and had resigned on 06.08.2020.

It is also submitted that between the Society and co-accused Dilip Sisodia, an MoU was executed on 01.11.2018 and an agreement to sale was also executed on 27.08.2019 of survey Nos.193, 194, 195, 196 and 197, a total area of 20,324 sq.ft. for construction of building with super built-up area of 50,000 sq.ft.

It is also submitted that due to some reasons, the sale deed of the aforementioned land has not been executed therefore, the applicant had returned a sum of Rs.70.00 lacs to the Society in November, 2019 and December,
2020.

It is also submitted that the Society through its Chairman has filed a Civil Suit No.RCSB/175/2022 for recovery of Rs.4,19,27,000/- with interest, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:32166 3 MCRC-28235-2024 which is pending before the Additional District Judge, Indore.
It is also submitted that the dispute is purely civil in nature therefore, no offence is made out against the applicant.
It is further submitted that prima-facie, no offence u/S 409 of IPC is made out against the applicant because applicant is not a public servant.
Counsel also submits that co-accused Dilip Sisodia has been granted regular bail by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order 15.07.2024 passed in MCRC No.29380/2024.

Applicant has no criminal past and is a reputed person and the police is trying to arrest him, if he gets arrested, his reputation will be tarnished therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be granted anticipatory bail.

To bolster his submission, he has placed reliance on the judgement of the Allahabad High Court in the case of Brijpal Singh V State of U. P. and another (Application u/S 482 No.45468/2023 dated 08.04.2024) as well as other case laws.

entities.text: Brijpal Singh V State of U. P. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that applicant and co-accused have embezzled huge amount of the Society and the alleged sale consideration has not been deposited in the bank account of the Society but was deposited in the personal bank account of the accused persons.

It is also submitted that relevant document with respect to sale of plots were not found in the record of the Society and the same were not registered documents as well as have not been written on the stamp paper.
The aforesaid document was executed between co-accused Prakash Giri, President on behalf of the Society and co-accused Ex-President Dilip Sisodia.

It is also submitted that co-accused Prakash Giri had filed the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:32166 4 MCRC-28235-2024 aforesaid Civil Suit on behalf of the Society for recovery of the amount therefore, it is clear that the aforesaid documents and civil suit was executed and filed by co-accused Prakash Giri to give civil color to the offence and save himself and the co-accused persons from the offence.
It is also submitted that at that relevant time, no audit of the Society was conducted by co-accused persons/executive members of the Society.

It is further submitted that co-accused persons Prakash Giri, Smt. Madhukanta Giri and Kamlesh Jain used to operate the bank accounts of the Society and they were also the signatories on behalf of the Society.

He further submits that earlier regular bail application of co-accused Dilip Sisodia was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 27.02.2024 passed in MCRC No.46273/2023 thereafter, Special Leave to Appeal (Cri.) No.4686/2024 against the aforesaid order was also dismissed as withdrawn by the Apex Court vide order dated 18.06.2024 but later on, co-accused Dilip Sisodia was granted regular Milan Giri vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117670516/
2 bail by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court on 15.07.2024.

sentences.text: The offence is serious in nature and custodial interrogation of the applicant is required therefore, on the ground that co-accused is granted regular bail, applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

5. In the case of Brijpal Singh (Supra), the Allahabad High Court in paragraph-21 has observed as under:-
"21.

Though it is correct that in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of State of Maharashtra vs. Laljit Rajshi Shah (supra) that an employee of the cooperative society is not a public servant under Section 21 of I.P.C. for offence u/s 409 I.P.C., he cannot be prosecuted under Section 409 I.P.C. as he is not a public servant.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra vs. Laljit Rajshi Shah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, this question can be raised at the time of framing of charge b e c a u s e e m p l o y e e s o f c o o p e r a t i v e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2024:MPHC-IND:32166 5 MCRC-28235-2024 society can be prosecuted for breach of trust."

6. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also looking to overall facts and circumstances of the case and as submitted by counsel for the State that custodial interrogation of the applicant required, this Court is of the view that it is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, this anticipatory bail application is dismissed.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE gp Milan Giri vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117670516/
